title: I Took the Laser-Tag Vest Recharge to the Manager Who Kept Extra Packs

parts.text: I checked vest 12 at 4:05 p.m. and manager Rex had three charged packs in a tote labeled SPARE STAFF. The desk said: ONE VEST. ONE PACK. RETURN ON THE BEEP. I was twenty-six, birthday booker, holding a waiver that listed one pack. Rex did not stop. "Managers are the arena." I photographed the tote, the desk, and his packs on my beep. Then I logged an overlap. At 4:12 the owner asked why Rex's tote was on my recharge. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Rex's spare packs on vest 12 during my recharge beep.

social.video_title: He kept three charged packs in a staff tote — Part 1/2
social.description: Laser tag, a manager's tote, and a one-pack desk he posted. I logged the overlap. Would you have knocked?

parts.text: Rex called it a spare until the owner asked for the log. I printed the overlap, the photo, and the waiver. He returned two packs. Rex booked his own beep and told hosts spares were always about optics. Optics is a word managers use when waivers exist. Recharge now has a second line: MANAGERS RETURN ON THE BEEP. I keep my one pack. Rex schedules. The arena finally sounds like a waiver, not a tote. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Managers return on the beep — Part 2/2
social.description: Overlap log, returned packs, and a second line. Was a spare ever my waiver?
